skip.description: True when no clear-cut improvement was made.

skip_reason.description: Why the proposer skipped, empty when proposing.

category.description: The one permitted kind of improvement.

title.description: A short commit subject for the improvement.

summary.description: What changed and why it improves the repository.

problem.description: What is wrong and why it matters, in plain words for a reader new to this repository: what the code does, what is hard or risky about it today, and who or what it affects. Two to five sentences; no jargon without a one-line explanation.

options.description: The ways to fix it that you weighed; one is enough for a simple problem. The first is the one you chose.

tradeoff.description: What it gains and what it costs or risks.

chosen.description: Why the first option was chosen over the others (or, with one option, why it is the obvious fix).

reading_guide.description: Breadcrumbs for a reader who does not know this code: which files and functions to read first and in what order, what concept to understand, and one or two good questions to ask the owner. Use repository-relative paths.

why_safe.description: Why the change stays within the owner's boundaries.

tests_run.description: Tests actually run and their results, never invented.

lens.description: The selected lens; equal to category.

claim.description: One falsifiable fact about the base code.

quote.description: Exact base excerpt; whitespace within a line may vary.

evidence.description: Evidence quoted from the base commit.

measurement.description: Before/after values and producing command for performance; empty otherwise.

edits.description: Exact text edits for Python to apply, in order. Each search must occur exactly once in the file at the base commit after earlier edits; an empty search creates a new file whose content is replace.

search.description: Exact existing text, copied character for character with enough lines to be unique; empty to create a file.
